title: Five Pacific islands lost to rising seas as climate change hits
description: Using time series aerial and satellite imagery from 1947 to 2014 of 33 islands, along with historical insight from local knowledge, we have identified five vegetated reef islands that have vanished over this time period and a further six islands experiencing severe shoreline recession.
longFormSummary:
• A 2016 study published in Environmental Research Letters examined how sea-level rise and wave exposure interact to erode low-lying reef islands in the Solomon Islands, a region with some of the highest rates of sea-level rise in the world.
  • Researchers analyzed aerial photographs from 1947-1962 and satellite imagery from 2002-2014 across 33 islands, combined with wave-energy hindcast data and radiocarbon dating of trees.
  • Five vegetated reef islands vanished entirely and six more lost over 20% of their area during the study period.
  • Erosion accelerated sharply on the more wave-exposed Isabel islands, where shoreline recession rates rose from about 0.1% annually (1947-1962) to 1.9% annually (2002-2014), compared with minimal change in the more sheltered Roviana region, where wave energy was twenty times lower.
  • At two Isabel sites, erosion destroyed villages that had existed since at least 1935, forcing community relocations.
  • The study concludes that sea-level rise and high wave exposure interact synergistically, meaning local wave conditions can dramatically amplify a coastline's vulnerability to climate-driven erosion.

title: Hivemapper is 1M kilometers closer to goal of beating Google Maps
description:
Hivemapper relied on ride-hail, delivery and truck drivers with dash cams to collect 1 million unique kms of fresh map data.

Hivemapper, the startup that puts dashcams on ride-hail and delivery vehicles to map the world, is getting a little closer to its goal of toppling the B2B mapping empire that Google has built.

With only 2% of the world’s roads mapped, Hivemapper is still very much the underdog in this fight. But Gabe Nelson, Hivemapper’s head of operations, reckons the startup is reaching an inflection point that will lead to exponential scale.

Its dashcams are equipped with a high-quality imager and precise GPS, and they go for $549. Mapping with dashcams, the company says, means its data is continuously being refreshed, whereas much of Google’s Street View imagery, particularly outside of urban centers, is over a decade old.

title: Halley's Comet Returns to Perihelion
description: The most famous comet swings back through the inner solar system on its 76-year orbit, having last appeared in 1986.
longFormSummary:
• Halley's Comet, officially designated 1P/Halley, is the only short-period comet consistently visible to the naked eye from Earth, a "dirty snowball" of ice and dust with a nucleus roughly 11 kilometers across.
  • It follows a highly elliptical, retrograde orbit lasting 74 to 79 years, swinging from a perihelion of just 0.59 astronomical units from the Sun out to an aphelion of 35 AU, nearly reaching Pluto's orbit.
  • Its appearances have been recorded since at least 240 BC in Chinese records, and its 1066 passage is depicted on the Bayeux Tapestry.
  • English astronomer Edmond Halley established its periodicity in 1705 by matching observations from 1531, 1607, and 1682, correctly predicting its return in 1758.
  • Having last appeared in February 1986, the comet is expected to return to the inner solar system around mid-2061, with its perihelion passage predicted for either July 28, 2061 or, under an alternate calculation accounting for gravitational perturbations, March 27, 2134.
